markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) SASRec already models ordered preferences through causal attention. A recent-history residual tests whether its final representation underweights current intent. (2) Users report stale interests and broadly related recommendations displacing specific matches. Recent conditioning addresses both hypotheses, but cannot establish compatibility or satisfied demand. (3) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. Stronger competition is justified as an experiment; these diagnostics neither establish its cause nor predict validation HR@10.

**Related-work insights.** (1) MSMT-LSI and HyperHawkes motivate short/long preference fusion without establishing benefits here. (2) SASRec’s normalized features require recency-branch scale control; ReZero motivates exact initial preservation. (3) gSASRec motivates multiple negatives, but sampled cross-entropy does not inherit gBCE calibration. R²NS supports caution about early hard mining. (4) Recommendation-evaluation guidance and selection-overfitting research motivate paired comparisons and fixed checkpoint opportunities.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Current intent | Short/long preference fusion | Zero-initialized gated recent residual |
| Ranking discrimination | Multiple-negative objectives | Uniform sampled-candidate cross-entropy |
| Joint adaptation | Intent-conditioned ranking | Recent residual with multiple negatives |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are judgments, not measured outcomes; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Recent residual | 3: targeted; familiar | 6: extensible; recency can mislead | 8: targets stale/broad matches; specificity remains latent | 4: may improve margins; indirect | 3: small module; scale/masking matter |
| B: Multiple-negative cross-entropy | 2: established; limited novelty | 7: stronger competition; sampling-sensitive | 4: sharper ranking; no intent mechanism | 8: targets wrong ranks; false negatives remain | 4: simple objective; exclusion/memory need care |
| C: Gated recent residual plus B | 4: diagnostic combination; familiar components | 7: adaptable; gains unverified | 8: targets both reported failures; utility unverified | 8: targets weak margins; HR uncertain | 5: modest architecture; integration substantial |

### Selected idea: C

At 0% progress, retain this feasible combination, with corrected initialization and sampling semantics. Compute a causal five-item mean with decay 0.7, normalize only this branch, and use h′=h+αP·LN(m), initially α=0 and P nonzero. This exactly preserves initial SASRec scores. Train with 32 uniform negatives sampled with replacement from items outside each user’s training history and current target. Preserve duplicates; optimize uncorrected sampled-candidate cross-entropy, without calibration claims.

Predeclare baseline/A/B/C, identical training/evaluation schedules, fixed-final-checkpoint ablations, and three baseline comparisons. Select deployment checkpoints by pinned macro validation HR@10; label best-checkpoint comparisons exploratory. Report category results, paired stratified bootstrap intervals, discordant users, and multiplicity-adjusted comparisons when per-user hits are available. Bootstrap intervals do not correct checkpoint selection.

Budget every run, diagnosis, and failure within 43,200 GPU-seconds. A last-item residual is a useful subsequent ablation, not an additional undeclared search. Preserve seeds, splits, routing, diagnostics, and predictor reconstruction. Popularity shortcuts, false negatives, and transient recency remain risks; no improvement or causal explanation is established.

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized scalar-gated recent-history residual to SASRec and train it with uniform multiple-negative sampled-candidate cross-entropy. At each valid position, add a projected, branch-normalized, exponentially weighted mean of up to five recent input-item embeddings to the original sequence feature. Compare baseline, residual-only, loss-only, and combined variants.
idea.motivation: The recent branch explicitly targets two reported user failures: historical interests overpowering current purpose, and broadly plausible associations displacing specific recent matches. Multiple-negative competition targets measured weak ranking separation, particularly Electronics’ 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate. These are mechanism hypotheses rather than demonstrated improvements. Neither mechanism establishes equipment compatibility, complementary function, whether a purchase satisfied a need, or unobserved simulator traits. The embedding similarity measurements do not justify treating representation collapse as the primary problem.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, original splits, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory and execute on one GPU. Do not access hidden test files or unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, or stores.

Architecture: preserve the baseline SASRec feature path, including its existing embedding scaling, normalization, causal mask, and padding behavior. For the recent branch, use raw shared item embeddings and m_t = sum_{j=0..4}(0.7^j * valid_{t-j} * e_{t-j}) / max(sum_{j=0..4}(0.7^j * valid_{t-j}), epsilon). Use explicit left padding or causal slicing, never wrapping tensor shifts. Include only input positions <= t, never the next-item target. Return zero for an empty window. Apply LayerNorm only to this branch, then a learned linear projection P. Define fused features as h_t + alpha * P(LN(m_t)), with alpha initialized to exactly zero and P initialized with ordinary nonzero weights. Initialize projection bias to zero; remask padding after normalization, projection, and fusion. Do not zero both alpha and P, which would block initial learning. The original negative-biased sigmoid convex gate only approximately preserved predictions and had uncontrolled branch scale; this residual replaces it. Shared dropout behavior still makes training predictions stochastic, but the residual contributes exactly zero at initialization for the same baseline forward pass. Keep temperature fixed at 1 and use unchanged shared item-dot-product scoring.

Objective: at every valid next-item position, sample k=32 negatives independently with replacement from real item IDs outside the user's complete training history and current target. Exclude padding and skip positions with no eligible negative. Training-history exclusion must not consult validation/test interactions. Repeated negative IDs remain repeated denominator terms; repeated targets remain separate sequence-position examples. The positive appears exactly once in column zero. Use cross-entropy over these 33 logits without logQ correction and describe it as a sampled-candidate ranking surrogate, not calibrated full-catalog sampled softmax or gBCE. The proposal is user-dependent, so identical uniform correction terms cannot simply be assumed to cancel against the deterministically inserted positive. Unobserved positives remain possible false negatives. Avoid in-batch candidate sharing in this initial experiment. Use bounded rejection sampling with an exact eligible-set fallback to avoid hangs for dense users.

Reduction and optimization: average loss over all eligible positions in a batch, not over chunk means. Backpropagate chunk loss sums divided by the batch's eligible-position count, retaining the shared feature graph until the final chunk when necessary; take one optimizer step per original batch. Start with the baseline optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and other hyperparameters unchanged. Record their resolved values, model initialization, random-generator states, negative-sampling configuration, and data fingerprints. Chunking must change memory use only, not the objective. The architecture is small, but rejection sampling, chunked gradients, and four-category predictor integration justify increasing code difficulty from 4 to 5.

Integration: save window, decay, LayerNorm, projection, scalar gate, and every baseline inference parameter in each category checkpoint. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the trained module and preserves dataset routing. Require reload parity for identical sequences and candidate IDs, padding-zero checks, and causal-prefix invariance before expensive training. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Keep view.model as the actual nn.Module, view.item_emb as its shared embedding, view.log2feats as fused feature computation, and view.predict_score identical to inference scoring. Preserve the (None, sequence, positive, negative) B x L loader contract. Return measured metrics and metric_definitions, and generate the interpretation prompt from both. Continue embedding-similarity and margin measurements with matched probe samples; mark category breakdowns unavailable because item categories are unavailable. Report diagnostic sample counts and avoid interpreting training margins as validation HR@10.

Evaluation: predeclare four variants: baseline with original loss; A with residual and original loss; B with original architecture and new loss; C with both. Keep initialization seeds, data order, pinned evaluation users/candidates, and evaluation schedules matched wherever feasible. Record separate RNG streams for model initialization, training sampling, and diagnostics so probes do not perturb training. Use the host's pinned 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Do not replace or modify its evaluator. Use common macro validation HR@10 for deployment selection. Use a predeclared final checkpoint for controlled ablation comparisons; report best-checkpoint results as exploratory and record every checkpoint opportunity. A cheap h'=h+alpha*LN(e_t) last-item residual, alpha=0, can isolate immediate-item signal in a subsequent explicitly budgeted experiment; it is not silently added to the initial four variants.

If the authorized evaluator exposes per-user validation hits, save binary hit@10 with user/category IDs, use 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates resampling 200 users within each category, and report macro differences with 95% intervals plus category differences and discordant-user counts. Predeclare the three baseline comparisons and use Holm-adjusted paired-test p-values, with exact paired discordance tests when their exchangeability assumptions are appropriate. Ordinary intervals remain pointwise unless simultaneous intervals are constructed. These analyses describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty and do not correct checkpoint or variant selection. If per-user hits are not exposed, report available host metrics and explicitly omit unavailable intervals rather than changing evaluation.

Compute and risks: allocate at most 10,000 GPU-seconds per variant, with a shared 3,200-second reserve for diagnostics, debugging, and failures; total charged work must never exceed 43,200 GPU-seconds. Unused allocations need not be spent. Retain the 200-epoch default, subject to each predeclared resource cap, and label capped runs as resource-limited. Compare matched training resources where caps prevent common epoch completion; do not present them as equal-epoch ablations. Keep equal checkpoint opportunities and stop by budget rather than statistical significance. Repeated validation selection can overfit 800 fixed validation users. Item popularity and broad lexical or collaborative associations may remain shortcuts; the recency branch itself does not enforce specific purpose. Recent purchases may also be transient noise or satisfied demand. Track the supplied user-facing rejection reasons only when actually observed; retain uncertain judgments separately. Future potential is reduced from 8 to 7 because the contribution is incremental and benefits remain unverified. No gains, significance, compatibility understanding, or held-out generalization are claimed before measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
class RecentResidualSASRec(SASRec):
    def __init__(self, ...):
        super().__init__(...)
        self.recent_norm = LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        self.recent_projection = Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
        initialize_nonzero_weights_and_zero_bias(self.recent_projection)
        self.alpha = Parameter(0.0)

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        h = super().log2feats(sequence)  # Preserve baseline path exactly.
        valid = sequence != 0
        e = self.item_emb(sequence)     # Raw shared input embeddings.
        numerator = zeros_like(e)
        denominator = zeros_like(valid, dtype=float)
        for lag in range(5):
            # Left shifts here mean explicit left padding, never cyclic roll.
            prior_e = causal_left_pad_shift(e, lag)
            prior_valid = causal_left_pad_shift(valid, lag)
            weight = (0.7 ** lag) * prior_valid
            numerator += weight[..., None] * prior_e
            denominator += weight
        m = numerator / clamp_min(denominator[..., None], epsilon)
        m = zero_where_empty(m, denominator)
        r = self.recent_norm(m)
        r = mask_padding(r, valid)
        r = self.recent_projection(r)
        r = mask_padding(r, valid)
        return mask_padding(h + self.alpha * r, valid)

for batch in training_batches:
    _, sequence, positive, _ = batch
    # Dataset/collator retains the aligned users' training-only exclusion sets.
    positions = eligible_positions(sequence, positive, batch_training_histories)
    if len(positions) == 0:
        continue
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    for chunk_index, chunk in enumerate(chunks(positions)):
        negatives = uniform_sample_with_replacement(
            k=32,
            exclude=padding_and_current_target_and_user_training_history,
            bounded_rejection_with_exact_fallback=True)
        candidates = concatenate(chunk.positive[:, None], negatives, axis=1)
        logits = item_dot_product(features[chunk.positions], candidates)
        loss = cross_entropy(logits, zero_target_column, reduction='sum')
        loss = loss / len(positions)
        loss.backward(retain_graph=not_last_chunk(chunk_index))
    optimizer.step()

# Predeclare baseline, A=residual, B=loss, C=both.
# Keep training configuration and evaluation opportunities matched.
# Fixed-final checkpoints support ablations; best validation checkpoints are exploratory.
# Select deployment using unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
# Save all architecture parameters and emit the matching routed predictor.
# Preserve diagnostic adapters; count all charged work against the shared budget.

originality.positive: Combines causal recent-interest adaptation, exact residual initialization, and stronger sampled competition in direct response to both supplied diagnoses.
originality.negative: Short/long preference fusion, zero-initialized residual gates, and multiple-negative objectives are established; their combination provides limited methodological novelty.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled foundation for timestamp-aware gates, last-item comparisons, or multiple recent interests if the initial ablations succeed.
future_potential.negative: The approach is incremental, recency can reinforce transient or satisfied demand, and sampled-margin gains may not improve fixed macro validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: The model adds only causal pooling, branch normalization, a projection, and one scalar while preserving shared item scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact initialization, user-aligned exclusion sets, correctly normalized chunked gradients, diagnostic adapters, predictor reconstruction, and budget accounting require substantial integration care.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and shared item-embedding scoring architecture.
The original implementation scales input embeddings by the square root of hidden dimension and normalizes final sequence features.
limitations: Its architecture alone does not guarantee that current specific intent dominates broad historical associations.
A new branch must respect baseline feature scale and masking; averaging embeddings alone does not preserve variance.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI (2024)
contributions: Separately models short- and long-term preferences and fuses their representations.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed minimal residual or this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)
contributions: Combines latent intents, recurrence modeling, and short-term attention mixtures.
limitations: Its richer machinery adds implementation and tuning cost; consumed-item recurrence cannot directly serve unseen-item recommendations.
Observed recurrence does not establish complementary utility or satisfied demand.

related_work.title: gSASRec extended abstract (2024)
contributions: Motivates multiple-negative training and generalized BCE calibration.
limitations: The proposed sampled-candidate cross-entropy is a different objective and does not inherit gBCE calibration claims.
History-excluding sampling differs from the official sampler's assumptions.

related_work.title: Corrected logQ work (RecSys 2025)
contributions: Examines sampling-distribution correction while accounting for deterministic inclusion of the positive.
limitations: Sampling correction does not resolve uncertain false negatives or establish current user intent.
A user-dependent, history-excluding proposal requires explicit support and positive-contribution semantics; a blanket uniform correction is insufficient.

related_work.title: R²NS (WWW 2026)
contributions: Motivates caution about aggressive hard-negative mining early in training.
limitations: Does not demonstrate that uniform negatives are optimal for these four datasets.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Motivates residual branches controlled by zero-initialized scalar gates.
limitations: Supports the initialization mechanism, not recommendation gains.
Zero-initializing both the scalar and residual projection would block their initial gradients.

related_work.title: Evaluating Recommendation Systems
contributions: Provides evaluation guidance supporting user-level comparisons and careful interpretation of recommendation metrics.
limitations: The proposed stratified paired bootstrap is an adaptation; it does not capture training-seed uncertainty, candidate-sampling uncertainty, or validation-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated optimization of a finite validation criterion can bias reported performance.
limitations: Multiplicity adjustment across variants alone does not remove checkpoint-selection optimism.
The fixed benchmark validation protocol provides no independent confirmation during search.

related_work.title: Hyperband: A Novel Bandit-Based Approach to Hyperparameter Optimization
contributions: Provides a principled framework for allocating limited training resources and predeclaring pruning schedules.
limitations: Resource allocation does not protect against validation reuse.
The initial proposal uses fixed allocations; any later successive-halving schedule must declare rungs and promotion counts before use.

related_work.title: Official PyTorch gSASRec sampler
contributions: Makes replacement sampling, duplicate negatives, and collision behavior explicit for implementation comparison.
limitations: The described official sampler does not exclude targets or user training histories; reproducing its sampling differs from the proposed history-excluding surrogate.

related_work.title: TensorFlow sampled softmax and uniform candidate sampling
contributions: Documents accidental-hit removal and expected-count correction semantics.
Companion candidate-sampler documentation distinguishes replacement sampling from unique sampling.
limitations: Automatic sampled-target collision handling does not exclude all other user positives.
These API semantics do not make the proposed uncorrected candidate cross-entropy calibrated.
